blocks.title: DeckCraft in the activity panel
blocks.description: Themes, layouts, shapes and charts — the upstream DeckCraft editor running inside Astravia, with the deck you opened in the workspace.

showcase.user_prompt: Open DeckCraft and turn the background of @assets/cover.png into a blue gradient.
showcase.assistant_reply: Cover loaded. Turning the background into a blue gradient now.

items.title: Slides, not a canvas
items.description: Each slide is a real layout with placeholders, so text, images and charts arrive in the right frame instead of being dragged pixel by pixel.

items.title: Decks that leave as .pptx
items.description: A deck opens from the workspace and exports back to it as PowerPoint, so the file you hand over opens in the tool the audience already has.

items.title: Ask which slide is on screen
items.description: A capture tool saves a PNG of what the canvas is showing and a status tool reports whether the editor finished starting.

items.title: Driven from the conversation
items.description: Ask in chat and the panel carries it out: pointer and keyboard steps run inside the editor one after another, each one named on the canvas while it happens.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: About 12 MB of editor files arrive on first open and are reused offline after that.

items.title: Open the DeckCraft tab
items.description: Opening the tab shows the editor itself — no preparation screen, no package to fetch.

items.title: Open a deck or start one
items.description: File → Open takes the file selected in Astravia; a new deck starts from a theme.

items.title: Export as .pptx through the workspace
items.description: Exports travel the same bridge as saves.

blocks.content: DeckCraft is young: expect missing PowerPoint features and changing files. The plugin runs the pinned release and adds no slide features of its own.

Automation is an ordinary operation, not a macro player: a batch is a list of pointer and key steps the editor receives exactly as if they came from a hand, paced by frames so a press lasts a press. The canvas reports a text map and its average colour back, which is how the agent checks that a change really happened before reporting it.
